subject: Coordination: Eval orchestration + MAP review for Acme AI promptset A/B
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@acmeai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Eval orchestration + MAP review for Promptset A/B

Hi Olivia —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We sketched a simple mutual action plan (MAP) to align on how Redwood will run an A/B eval of your prompt variants and validate guardrails before rollout. I attached a draft MAP and the promptset files for A and B.

High-level asks for Acme:
- Confirm target success metrics (exact pass/fail thresholds)
- Provide 100 representative queries (anonymized) by 4/13
- Identify any safety-sensitive categories that must be flagged

From our side we propose:
- A 2-week A/B run in staging with automatic signal collection (latency, token-cost, accuracy proxies)
- Primary acceptance criteria: no >3% negative quality regression on the signal set + no safety hits above your threshold

Can you confirm the metrics and the timeline? Once you confirm I’ll loop in Marissa and Jonas to finalize eval instruments and the canary gating plan.

Thanks,
Priyom
Priyom Das
Head of Product Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Acme_MAP_v1.xlsx (attachment), promptset-A-vs-B.json (attachment)

From: Olivia Park <olivia@acmeai.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-11T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Eval orchestration + MAP review for Promptset A/B

Hi Priyom —

Thanks — this looks good. Quick clarifications:
1) For pass/fail, can we define "negative quality regression" as drop in our human-evaluated correctness score (0-100) relative to baseline? 3% seems reasonable but we might ask for ~2% on some high-value intents.
2) We can deliver anonymized queries by EOD 4/13.
3) Safety categories: financial-advice & PII handling — please flag those.

If you need me to route anything to procurement for the staging capacity, let me know.

—Olivia
Olivia Park
Head of Product, Acme AI

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-12T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: Acme MAP + eval plan (need quick turn)

Team —

Acme confirmed timeline and safety categories. They want 2-week A/B in staging, deliver queries 4/13. Key asks for us:
- Marissa: please draft evaluation rubric and acceptance criteria doc that maps human scores -> pass/fail thresholds and edge-case escalation rules. Include examples for the financial-advice and PII intents.
- Jonas: propose canary gating rules (traffic splits, rollback thresholds, automated fallback). We need a decision tree for what happens at 1%, 2%, 3% regressions.
- Dev: list any runtime constraints (batching, tokenization differences) that might affect metric comparability between prompt variants. Also confirm whether we can enable prefix caching for this run.

I attached the MAP and prompt files — start with those. We have a call Friday 4/15 10:00 PT with Acme to finalize. Please reply with a short plan by EOD tomorrow so I can share with Olivia.

Thanks —
Priyom

Attachments: eval-acceptance-criteria.md (draft), Acme_MAP_v1.xlsx (attachment)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-13T15:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Acme MAP + eval plan (need quick turn)

+1 on the timeline. Quick notes from the evaluation side:

Acceptance criteria (draft):
- Primary signal: human correctness score drop relative to baseline <= 2.5% (weighted by intent importance).
- Secondary signals: automated NLU heuristics (intent misclass rate) should not increase >1.5%; safety hits must be 0 for PII and <0.5% for financial-advice flagged by our classifier.
- Operational: latency percentile (p95) must not degrade >20% and cost/token increase must be <12%.

Escalation flow:
1) If primary signal breaches 1.5% -> notify Marissa + CS and pause canary expansion.
2) If primary signal breaches 2.5% or safety breaches -> automatic rollback to baseline and immediate incident postmortem.

Questions for Dev: are we able to run both variants with identical runtime conditions (same batcher config) to make the human scores comparable? If not, we should instrument a normalization factor.

I can convert this to the acceptance doc and push to the MAP. Attaching a short checklist.

—Marissa
Senior Product Manager, Evals

Attachments: eval-acceptance-criteria.md (updated)

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-04-14T10:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Acme MAP + eval plan (need quick turn)

FW: tech constraints and proposal —

We can run both variants under the same runtime if we pin the model binary and use deterministic batching config. Caveats:
- Prompt A uses a longer average prefix which will increase token cost; we should normalize by per-query token usage when reporting cost deltas.
- Prefix caching can be enabled but only if we run the A/B in isolation per-client session ID; mixing traffic will reduce cache hit parity.
- We will instrument a traffic tag so each response includes: variant_id, model_revision, batching_id, and token_count. That will allow offline normalization of human scores.

I added a short ops runbook and a stub for the canary automation (will push to the shared doc). No blockers from infra; timeline looks good.

—Dev
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

Attachments: ops-canary-runbook.md (attachment)

From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>

Olivia —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Latest from our internal sync:
- Marissa attached the acceptance criteria (primary threshold = 2.5% weighted human score drop; escalation triggers at 1.5% and automatic rollback at 2.5% + any safety hit).
- Dev confirmed we can run identical runtime conditions and will emit normalization metadata.
- I updated the MAP with responsibilities and timelines; see the attached Acme_MAP_v1.xlsx.

Next steps for Friday 4/15 10:00 PT call:
- Walk through acceptance criteria and any intent-weighting you want to apply.
- Confirm the 100-query set and safety labels.
- Finalize who will own post-run analysis and SLA for corrections.

If that works, we’ll route the staging quota and toggle the canary automation after sign-off.

Cheers,
Priyom
Head of Product Partnerships, Redwood Inference
